newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures pare initial losses, ignore BOJ move.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures pare initial losses, ignore BOJ move.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were virtually flat in early Tokyo trade on Thursday, after opening down in line with an overnight fall on LIFFE, traders said.
June was down 0.02 at 126.74 as of 9.51 a.m. (0051 GMT), after earlier falling as low as 126.56.

The key contract fell as low as 126.47 on Wednesday's LIFFE session after senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said in a speech that there was political pressure to raise the official discount rate.

"Some politicians have called for a rise in the official discount rate. It is true that there is an atmosphere among politicians to raise the official discount rate," said Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's international finance bureau.

"JGB futures quickly recovered after an initial fall triggered by Sakakibara's remarks. The impact was short-lived as it is unlikely that Japan will raise interest rates in the near future," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
Bargain-hunting by investors was detected after earlier weakness, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.160 percent, up from 2.150 percent on Wednesday. It rose as high as 2.175 percent earlier.
Slower-than-expected money supply growth was also supportive for JGBs, traders said.
Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs) grew a preliminary 2.7 percent year-on-year in March, compared with 3.0 percent growth in February.
Economists' money supply growth forecasts had ranged from 2.8 to 3.1 percent.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) drained a net 200 billion yen from the money market on Thursday. The market was in surplus by about 290 billion yen going into the day.
The BOJ's move was less accommodative than expected, but it had little impact on JGBs, bond traders said.
Money traders had expected the central bank either to drain about 100 billion yen or to refrain from conducting operations.
